cases.sentence: «Это лихорадка, – подумал я. – Этот ___ повсюду – от лихорадки, потому что сам я в ознобе, а повсюду жаркий туман».
cases.explain: «жаркий туман» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: ‘Ive got a fever,’ I thought, "this hot fog everywhere, it’s from a fever because I’m shivering myself and there’s hot fog everywhere. And someone very familiar appears from out of the fog, Achilles—not Achilles but very familiar. Oh, now I see, it’s the Pontic King Mithridates, all smeared with snot, with a penknife in his hand . .

cases.explain: «понтийский царь» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: ‘Ive got a fever,’ I thought, "this hot fog everywhere, it’s from a fever because I’m shivering myself and there’s hot fog everywhere. And someone very familiar appears from out of the fog, Achilles—not Achilles but very familiar. Oh, now I see, it’s the Pontic King Mithridates, all smeared with snot, with a penknife in his hand . .

cases.explain: «понтийский царь» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: ‘It is I,’ the Pontic King answered.

cases.explain: «другие дни» — after the preposition «в», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.

cases.sentence: «Изувер!» И тут мне пронзило ___, и я тихонько застонал, потому что не было во мне силы даже рукою защититься от ножика…
cases.explain: «левый бок» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: I was hit by the shivers once more. "What are you up to, Mithridates?"’ I whispered or cried, I don’t know which. "Get rid of the knife, what do you need with a knife?"’ But he couldn’t hear anything anymore. He threatened me; it was as if a thousand devils possessed him. "Savage!"’

cases.sentence: Но тут мне пронзило ___, потом опять левый, опять правый, – я успевал только бессильно взвизгивать, – и забился от боли по всему перрону.
cases.explain: «правый бок» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: But he stabbed me in the right side, then the left again, then the night. I only succeeded in screaming helplessly and rushing about the platform in pain. I woke up with cramps all over. There was nothing around except the wind, the dark, and devilish cold. "‘What’s with me and where am I? Why is it drizzling? Oh, God... ."’

cases.sentence: Вокруг – ничего, кроме ветра, тьмы и ___.
cases.explain: «собачьего холода» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: But he stabbed me in the right side, then the left again, then the night. I only succeeded in screaming helplessly and rushing about the platform in pain. I woke up with cramps all over. There was nothing around except the wind, the dark, and devilish cold. "‘What’s with me and where am I? Why is it drizzling? Oh, God... ."’

cases.sentence: Ты же сам говорил ___: „Раз-два-туфли надень-ка как-ти-бе-не стыдна-спать…“ Самое главное – уйди от рельсов, здесь вечно ходят поезда, из Москвы в Петушки, из Петушков в Москву.
cases.explain: «больному мальчику» — the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: ‘It’s nothing, Erofeev, nothing. Talife cumi, as your Tsaritsa said when you were lying in your coffin; that is, arise, brush off your coat, clean up your pants, shake the dust off, and go on. Try two steps, anyway, the rest will be easier. You yourself told your little boy when he was sick, ‘One-two-button-your-shoe, aren ’t-you-ashamed-to- be-lying-in-bed .. .. The main thing is to get off the tracks; trains are always going by here, from Moscow to Petushki, from Petushki to Moscow. Get off the tracks. Then you'll find out why there’s not a soul around and why she didn’t meet you and everything. Go on, Venichka, go on.
